question: How will the total energy of an electron in hydrogen atom change when it moves from the first orbit to the fourth orbit? Justify your answer.

options.A: The total energy decreases from $-13.6\text{ eV}$ to $-0.85\text{ eV}$ because higher orbits have more negative energy.
options.B: The total energy remains $-13.6\text{ eV}$ because the electron stays bound to the nucleus.
options.C: Using $E_n=-\dfrac{13.6}{n^2}\text{ eV}$, $E_1=-13.6\text{ eV}$ and $E_4=-\dfrac{13.6}{16}=-0.85\text{ eV}$. Thus, the total energy increases by $12.75\text{ eV}$ because it becomes less negative in the fourth orbit.
options.D: The total energy becomes zero in the fourth orbit, so the electron is ionised.
